Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Giovanni Giorgio Trissino (author, Wikidata Q436738), died 1550; Gilles Corrozet (editor, Wikidata Q3106164), died 1568; Mellin de Saint-Gelais (translator, Wikidata Q1361688), died 1558. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Trissino, Giovanni Giorgio, 1478-1550; Corrozet, Gilles, 1510-1568 [Editor]; Saint-Gelais, Mellin de, 1491-1558 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: uvres complètes de Melin de Sainct-Gelays, Paris, P. Daffis, 1873, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/uvrescompltesd03sain. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 47%, 69%, 44% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Giovanni Giorgio Trissino, Gilles Corrozet, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
